page: Amazon Web Services x8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered on the AWS Nitro System, targeted at data-intensive enterprise workloads. The system is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running on the x86_64 architecture with a maximum clock rate of 3.9 GHz. The setup provisions 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs alongside an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates comprehensive vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (tile and int8), facilitating acceleration for complex integer and floating-point computations.

Memory capacity is a defining characteristic of the x8i.24xlarge, featuring 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Benchmark evaluations reflect exceptional throughput across cache-bound and parallel execution paths, with small-block cached memory reads reaching 7680.48 GB/sec and multi-core Geekbench scores placing in the top tier at 22004.0. The instance delivers 171.86 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and demonstrates top-tier LLM prompt-processing speeds on small and medium parameter models utilizing AMX instructions.

The hardware configuration lacks local bundled storage, mandating reliance on external network-attached storage architectures. Networking bandwidth is baselined at 40 Gbps, ensuring high-throughput interconnection to external volumes and distributed systems. From an efficiency perspective, the high ratio of RAM to CPU delivers substantial resource density, maximizing throughput for memory-resident platforms without paying for unneeded accelerator hardware.

This server profile is structured specifically for in-memory databases like Redis and SAP HANA, large-scale data analytics, in-memory caching tiers, electronic design automation, and CPU-based matrix operations.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Featuring 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs running up to 3.9 GHz, and 480 MB of L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance supplies 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core compute capability, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 107115.33 and over 171 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance includes a 40 Gbps baseline network link, has zero bundled local storage, and contains no discrete GPUs. The substantial memory footprint and high memory bandwidth make it well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching clusters, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads.
